The ratio of any two classes (e.g. 0.91 vs 1.03) is read from paired intervals if analysis supplies them, else from the separate intervals, which do not overlap here.\n"+b,1)
c="With the larger-gap inner split (held-out share 0.5) the tuned one is 0.763, below fixed λ = 1 and below `balanced|calreg` (0.772): the shrinkage is a property of the nested design, not of λ-tuning as such;"

shown.message:
I took all three review points into the outline (revision 11) and closed `story-repo`#6.

- **Headline wording:** the headline now names the winning cell as source-informed balanced selection with a source-calibrated regression. It gives intervals against stratified sampling:

  | Cell | Ratio to stratified | 95% interval |
  |---|---|---|
  | `balanced\|calreg` | 0.91 | [0.89, 0.93] |
  | difference correction, selected | 1.03 | [0.99, 1.05] |
  | difference correction, post hoc | 0.96 | [0.93, 0.98] |

  I also added what the data say about which part does the work. `balanced|mean` is 0.95 of stratified, and calibrated regression on a stratified or uniform sample is worse than the plain mean (1.17 and 1.23). So the gain needs the pairing of balanced selection with calibration. The text says sources are used in the winning cell.
- **Class-level selection:** leave-one-benchmark-out picks `balanced|calreg` on every held-out benchmark. Naming that class as the winner is still a second, post-hoc step among five classes. The paper will show all five class rows and say 0.91 is the best of them.
- **`inner50`:** the 0.763 vs 0.772 difference stays out of the text. The evidence is the move from 0.815 [0.786, 0.837] to 0.763 [0.740, 0.781]. Those are separate bootstrap intervals, so I asked analysis on `experiment-repo`#5 for a paired interval of that move.

The recalibrated-estimator results and the R = 100 bias run are still open on that request.
